draft.title: Species with outsized effects
card: Some species have a much larger effect on their ecosystem than their numbers or body size would suggest. The effect reaches the whole community, not just the species itself.
If such a species is removed, other species can change a great deal. Some may increase sharply, and others may decline or disappear.
A top predator can be one of these species. It can hold down the numbers of its prey, which stops those prey from overusing food or habitat.

Example: sea otters eat sea urchins. Urchins graze on kelp, so with otters present, kelp forests can thrive and shelter many other species. If otters are lost, urchins can increase and strip the kelp.
draft.remember: A species can matter far more than its numbers, so losing it can reshape the whole community.

a.q: Which statement best describes a species that shapes its ecosystem far beyond its numbers?
opts: Removing it would change many other species in the community
It has the largest population in the ecosystem
It feeds on every other species in the community
It survives in a wider range of habitats than others
a.why: What marks this kind of species is its effect on the community, which is far greater than its numbers suggest. Having the largest population is a tempting idea, but such species are often not the most numerous.
a.clue: Think about effect compared with numbers, not population size.

b.q: A wetland has a few dingoes that hunt feral goats. Goats overgraze shoreline plants that shelter many insects and birds. The dingoes are removed. What is the most likely result?
opts: Goats increase and shoreline plants decline
Goats decline and shoreline plants grow back thicker
Little changes, because dingoes are few in number
Only dingoes are affected, as other species stay the same
b.why: The dingoes hold down goat numbers, so without them goats can increase and overgraze the plants that shelter other species. Few dingoes does not mean a small effect, because such a species can shape the community far beyond its numbers.
b.clue: Few in number does not mean small in effect.

a.best: Removing it would change many other species in the community

b.best: Goats increase and shoreline plants decline
